prompt: A protocol claims unforgeability but never defines adversary capabilities. Identify the missing security game.

Approach A requires a trusted setup, while approach B forbids it. Explain whether they can be combined without changing assumptions.
A reviewer says a protocol is insecure solely because it has a public verification key. Critically assess the objection.
Explore a new anonymous primitive without an existing formal specification. Identify definitions and research steps, not unproved claims.
An anonymous credential proof omits colluding corrupt verifiers. Identify missing security definitions.
A proof asserts that IND-CPA encryption automatically implies CCA2 security. Identify the invalid implication.
A proposal labels a construction novel although it resembles a supplied source. Describe the necessary comparison.
One protocol assumes honest parties, another malicious parties. Explain why composition needs unified threat assumptions.
A critic says a zero-knowledge proof must reveal its witness to be verified. Assess the objection.
A requested security primitive has no formal syntax. Develop a cautious roadmap with explicit unknowns.
